title: Cut boundary: points, edges and the leading-order witness geometry

key_results.statement: With no boundary, $\partial A=\emptyset$, the evolution factorizes, $e^{-iC\lambda}=U_A(\lambda)\otimes U_{\bar A}(\lambda)$ with $U_A=e^{-iC_A\lambda}$ and $U_{\bar A}=e^{-iC_{\bar A}\lambda}$; a product state stays a product, so $V_A$ is pure, $X_V$ is a single point and there is no edge, for every $\lambda$.
If $\partial A=\emptyset$, then for any admissible initial state $V_A(\lambda)=U_A(\lambda)\,V_A(0)\,U_A(\lambda)^\dagger$, so the spectrum of $V_A$ does not depend on $\lambda$.

The generalized record vector is $\lvert u_h\rangle=\frac{1}{\phi_h}\,Q_\chi\bigl(\langle h\rvert\otimes\mathbb 1_{\bar A}\bigr)C_\partial\bigl(\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle\bigr)$ with $Q_\chi=\mathbb 1_{\bar A}-\lvert\chi\rangle\langle\chi\rvert$; it depends only on $C_\partial$, $\phi$ and $\chi$, not on $C_A$, $C_{\bar A}$ or the decomposition of $C_\partial$.

For the initial state $\lvert\phi\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$ with $\phi_h\neq0$, $\lim_{\lambda\to0^+}\alpha(h,h';\lambda)/\lambda=d_0(h,h')=\lVert u_h-u_{h'}\rVert$, independent of $C_A$ and $C_{\bar A}$.
Every generalized record vector is orthogonal to $\chi$: $\langle\chi\vert u_h\rangle=0$ for every place $h$.

If every $A_n$ is diagonal in the place basis of $A$, then $\lvert u_h\rangle=\bigl(K_h-\langle K_h\rangle\bigr)\lvert\chi\rangle$ with $K_h=\sum_n\langle h\vert A_n\vert h\rangle B_n$, the record vector of (5.10).

If the $u_h$ are pairwise distinct and $\max\bigl(d_0(x,y),d_0(y,x')\bigr)\neq d_0(x,x')$ for all distinct $x,y,x'$, then for small $\lambda>0$ every place is a point, every two points are related, and $x\sim x'$ if and only if no $y$ has $\max\bigl(d_0(x,y),d_0(y,x')\bigr)<d_0(x,x')$ (the relative-neighbourhood graph of $\{u_h\}$).

For the internal term $C_A=t\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\bigl(\lvert h_i\rangle\langle h_{i+1}\rvert+\lvert h_{i+1}\rangle\langle h_i\rvert\bigr)$ on $a$ and every real $t$, $d_0(h_i,h_j)=\bigl\lVert(K_{h_i}-\langle K_{h_i}\rangle)\chi-(K_{h_j}-\langle K_{h_j}\rangle)\chi\bigr\rVert$, the value of (5.10).

If the only contract is $C=\bigl(\lvert h_1\rangle\langle h_2\rvert+\lvert h_2\rangle\langle h_1\rvert\bigr)\otimes B$, then $d_0(h_1,h_2)=\Bigl\lvert\frac{\phi_{h_2}}{\phi_{h_1}}-\frac{\phi_{h_1}}{\phi_{h_2}}\Bigr\rvert\,\sigma_\chi(B)$.

With $\phi_{h_2}/\phi_{h_1}=\rho e^{i\beta}$ and $\sigma_\chi(B)>0$, $d_0(h_1,h_2)^2=\bigl[(\rho-\rho^{-1})^2+4\sin^2\beta\bigr]\sigma_\chi(B)^2$, which vanishes if and only if $\phi_{h_2}=\pm\phi_{h_1}$.
In example (b), $W(h_1,h_2;\lambda)=1$ for every $\lambda$ when $\phi_{h_1}=\pm\phi_{h_2}$, so $h_1\approx h_2$: one point and no edge, although $\partial A\neq\emptyset$.

open_issues: Identical-type objects inside A (two objects of one type with at least two places): for a sign-changing type no admissible φ is nonzero on every place, so the hypothesis of item 2 cannot hold; for a swap-invariant type swapped places have equal record vectors, so the distinctness hypothesis of item 3 fails; items 2 and 3 on places are therefore informative only if A has no two objects of a common type with at least two places, and a version on classes of places is not derived.
Ties in the condition of item 3, higher orders in λ, finite λ beyond items 1 and 4(b), and initial states correlated across the cut are out of scope.
Comparison with the expected result: no discrepancy; the only addition is that W ≡ 1 also holds when the two amplitudes are opposite, φ(h₁) = −φ(h₂) (11.16).

consistency_checks.check: Scaling: under C → sC and λ → λ/s the state and α are unchanged; by (11.6) the record vectors scale with s, so d₀ scales with s and λd₀ is invariant, as it must be for an angle; in (11.13) the prefactor is dimensionless and σ(sB) = |s|σ(B).
With a vanishing boundary contract, (11.6) gives all record vectors zero, so d₀ ≡ 0, in agreement with item 1(a), where W ≡ 1 and α ≡ 0 exactly.

Example (b), exact against first order: expanding (11.15) gives ψ(h₁) = φ(h₁)χ − iλφ(h₂)Bχ + O(λ²), which is (11.5) with c₁(h₁) = φ(h₂)/φ(h₁); for φ(h₁) = ±φ(h₂) the exact branch vectors coincide up to sign, consistent with d₀ = 0 from (11.13).
